content.text:
[TASK]
Create one inferred Map destination window for the Japanese RPG prototype. It appears only after the existing Basic Info map button is clicked. Match the source application's exact late-1990s raster UI language without pretending this state was visible in the authority screenshot.

[REFERENCE ROLE]
Reference image 1 is the immutable full Japanese RPG screenshot and fixes the pixel scale, blue-grey palette, stepped window corners, title chrome, line weight, and overall source identity. Reference image 2 is the exact 280 by 150 card-window crop and fixes the requested output size and outer-window geometry. Reference image 3 is the exact Status window crop and reinforces the source title bar, one-pixel bevel hierarchy, compact density, and Japanese application character.

[PRESERVATION INVARIANTS]
- Use an exact 280 by 150 source-scale window silhouette with the same six-pixel stepped corners and 18-pixel title bar rhythm as the references.
- Keep hard aliased source-scale pixels, restrained blue-grey surfaces, one-pixel dark rules, and no modern UI styling.
- The window must be visually plausible beside the existing screenshot windows but remain a new inferred interaction state.
- Do not copy surrounding magenta desktop pixels or any neighboring source window.

[CANVAS AND LAYOUT]
- Return only the Map window at exactly 1120*600 pixels, four times the authoritative 280 by 150 source scale.
- No margin, desktop background, neighboring UI, caption, contact sheet, or review annotation.
- The complete window must fit the canvas with resolved stepped corners and no crop.

[REGION EDITS]
- REGION: title bar
  CHANGE: Render the exact Japanese title マップ once in the source pixel style, with one small source-matched title icon at left and one source-matched close button at right.
  PRESERVE: 18-pixel source title height; blue-grey title gradient; one-pixel outer chrome; clear separation between title text, icon, and close button
- REGION: map body
  CHANGE: Render a compact top-down fantasy town map inside a beveled white-and-pale-blue body panel. Use crisp one-pixel roads, a river, bridges, small building blocks, a player marker, and a thin source-themed border. Include no body text so no unreadable Japanese glyphs can be introduced.
  PRESERVE: clear body margins; source-scale pixel density; flat limited palette; independently croppable title and body regions

[EXACT COPY]
- title bar: "マップ"

[STYLE SYSTEM]
- Authentic Japanese late-1990s desktop RPG raster UI, matching the references rather than a modern retro interpretation.
- Hard source-scale pixels, pale blue-grey chrome, thin navy rules, compact dithered fantasy map art, and no antialiasing.

[ASSET RULES]
- Exactly one complete 280 by 150 Map window.
- Exactly one title icon, one マップ title, one close button, and one map body.
- Keep the title, icon, close button, map body, and empty chrome visually separable for later component extraction.

[NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS]
- No English MAP label, no gibberish, no additional Japanese body text, no duplicated title, no extra buttons, tabs, sliders, checkboxes, inventory items, character portraits, or dialogue.
- No magenta desktop, screenshot overlay, neighboring window, full game screen, modern rounded card, glass, blur, glow, soft shadow, antialiased typography, or high-resolution illustration style.
- Do not reuse the card illustration or Status statistics as map content.

[QUALITY GATE]
- At 280 by 150 the title reads exactly マップ and every glyph remains legible in the source pixel aesthetic.
- The outer silhouette and title geometry align with the 280 by 150 card reference.
- The map body contains no text and remains readable as a compact top-down town map at source scale.
- The output can be decomposed into an empty plate, title/icon/button components, and an independent map-body component without retaining a screenshot underlay.
